data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 asserts reliability is the inverse of catastrophic-failure probability rather than mean accuracy, but it provides no causal mechanism connecting a static checklist administered by non-experts to a reduced probability of catastrophic omission. A static checklist can only prompt verification of anticipated failure modes; it has no causal power to detect omissions the checklist author did not foresee. The target's own countercondition (checklist mirrors expert blind spots) concedes this, yet the core claim still assumes deterministic verification follows from checklist use. Without specifying how the checklist comes to cover the catastrophic-error space better than the expert's intuition, the reliability claim is asserted, not causally derived.
